# WO-2026-08-10-15 — The board is never wrong about being blocked
# guidance: WO-YYYY-MM-DD-nn — slice title

## Acceptance criteria

### The board says nothing is blocking a shop that cannot move

WP-B15-09 gave Warwick one board, edited in place, that tells him what is outstanding, what he has
answered, and **whether anything is blocking the shop**. It cleared a Gate 2 `FAIL`. It has a hole,
found by WP-B15-10 while proving a different point:

- `boardStateOf` (`runtime.js:1096`) derives `blocked` from `outstanding.length > 0`, where
  `outstanding` is question rows with `status === 'open'`.
- `planOutcome` (`stages.js:337-355`) reaches `AWAIT_LINE_RESOLUTION` **only after** `openQuestions > 0`
  has already returned — i.e. **precisely when zero questions are open.**

**So in the one state where a shop is parked on unresolved LINES, the board either does not exist
(`queueBoard` returns `{queued:false, reason:'no questions'}`) or renders `blocked: false` —
positively asserting that nothing is blocking a shop that CANNOT reach `READY_TO_SHOP`.**

That is the board **saying the wrong thing**, not merely saying nothing, and it is the exact class
Veritas failed Gate 2 on: *Warwick must be able to tell from the product whether he is stuck.* A
board that says "nothing is blocking" while the shop is parked is worse than the eight cards it
replaced, because he would believe it.

**This is why `lines_unresolved` was NOT retired.** WP-B15-10 was instructed to retire it, refused
with evidence, and was right: it is the only voice for the stuck state. Retiring it would have
restored a silent park. **Do not retire it here either** — the fix is to make the board TRUE, after
which its relationship to that card can be reconsidered by somebody with both facts.

### The second defect: a test harness that models intent instead of SQL

WP-B15-10's own mutation exposed this. Inverting its exclusion statement to the allowlist direction
— the very bug it had just reverted — left **every behavioural test green**; only a statement-shape
test went red.

Cause: `test/fakePg.js` has no handler for the statement, so the harness in `runPipeline.test.js`
answers it by matching the exported SQL constant and then applying **its own hardcoded semantics**.
It models what the query is *meant* to do, not what it *says*. Every behavioural test built on it is
blind to the statement's actual text.

### Acceptance criteria

**AC1 — THE BOARD IS NEVER WRONG ABOUT BEING BLOCKED.** When a shop cannot progress — including when
it is parked on unresolved lines with zero open questions — the board must not assert that nothing
is blocking it. **Establish the full set of parked states from `stages.js` rather than fixing only
the one named above**; `planOutcome` is the authority on what parks a shop, and a fix that repairs
`AWAIT_LINE_RESOLUTION` alone while another park state still renders `blocked: false` has moved the
defect, not closed it. `stages.js` is READ-ONLY to you — read it, do not edit it.

**AC2 — SILENCE IS NOT AN ACCEPTABLE ANSWER EITHER.** `queueBoard` returning `{queued:false,
reason:'no questions'}` leaves Warwick with nothing at all in exactly the state he most needs
telling. Whether the board should exist for a question-less parked shop is yours to propose; what is
NOT acceptable is a shop parked with no voice.

**AC3 — DO NOT RETIRE `lines_unresolved`.** It is currently the only voice for the stuck state, and
its disjointness from the board is pinned by tests. If your fix makes it genuinely redundant, SAY
SO and leave it standing; retirement is a separate decision with two files outside your surface.

**AC4 — `fakePg` MODELS THE EXCLUSION STATEMENT.** Add a handler to `test/fakePg.js` derived from the
SQL itself, so the whole suite becomes sensitive to the statement's text rather than to a
hand-written restatement of its intent. **Prove it works the only way that counts: invert the
statement to `shop_id = $1` and show that BEHAVIOURAL tests now go red**, not merely the shape test.
That inversion is the exact mutation that survived; it must not survive again.

**AC5 — REGRESSIONS FIRST, RED BEFORE GREEN**, for AC1 and AC4 both. Quote both directions with
executed counts.

**AC6 — MUTATION-PROVEN.** Mutate the AC1 guard, prove a NAMED test RED, restore byte-identical with
sha256 quoted both sides. **Assert the source actually changed before trusting any red** — three
workers hit silent no-op mutations in this build, one produced a vacuous green that looked entirely
orderly, and the harness pattern that caught it is worth reusing verbatim:
`if (!s.includes(from)) throw …; if (out === s) throw …`. Split on `/\r?\n/`, never `'\n'`.

**AC7 — NOTHING LIVE.** `live_authority: none`, `network: none`, `credential_scope: none`. No live
database. `SHOP-2026-08-09` and `SHOP-2026-08-10-M64` are both preserved and untouched.

## Required evidence

- `cd services/asdair/pipeline && node --test` -> PASS/FAIL counts before and after (baseline at this head: 444)
- `cd services/asdair/bot && node --test` -> counts before and after (baseline 183) — the board renders through bot/renderMessages.js, which is READ-ONLY to you
- the AC5 regressions in BOTH directions, each with executed counts
- the AC4 proof: invert the statement to `shop_id = $1` and quote the BEHAVIOURAL tests that now fail
- the AC6 mutation: named test RED, sha256 before and after restore, byte-identical
- `bash scripts/secret-scan.sh --surface services/asdair/pipeline/runtime.js services/asdair/pipeline/runtime.test.js services/asdair/pipeline/test/fakePg.js` → report exit code AND coverage. Exit 2 is NOT SCANNED, never a pass

## Inputs supplied

- `services/asdair/pipeline/runtime.js` — `boardStateOf` (~1096) and `queueBoard`. Yours.
- `services/asdair/pipeline/stages.js` — `planOutcome` (~337-355), the authority on what parks a shop. **READ-ONLY.**
- `services/asdair/pipeline/shopLines.js` — `SELECT_FOREIGN_CLAIMS_SQL`, the statement `fakePg` must model. **READ-ONLY.**
- `services/asdair/pipeline/runPipeline.test.js` — `withForeignClaimStatement`, the harness that models intent instead of SQL. **READ-ONLY and another worker's file**; your handler belongs in `test/fakePg.js`, and if the harness must then change, SAY SO rather than editing it.
- `Builds/BUILD-015-.../Assurance/veritas-phase-b15-user-journey-gate2-e0667dc.md` — the Gate 2 FAIL whose finding this defect partially re-opens.

## Explicitly out of scope — report, never fix

- Retiring `lines_unresolved` (AC3). It is the only voice for the stuck state.
- `stages.js`, `shopLines.js`, `runPipeline.js`, `bot/**` — read them; edit none. `runPipeline.js` is WP-B15-14's ACTIVE surface right now.
- `skill/termMatch.js` and `interpret/resolveByCatalogue.js` — WP-B15-13 is live on those.
- Redesigning the board. Make it truthful; do not re-open its shape.
- Repairing either live shop.

## Sequencing

1. **READ-BACK FIRST, then HOLD** (SOP-022). Enumerate every parked state `planOutcome` can reach and
   say which of them the board currently mis-reports — that enumeration is the real scope of AC1 and
   I want to see it before you build. Do not implement until Larry accepts or amends.
2. AC5 regressions RED first, for the board and for the `fakePg` handler.
3. AC1 and AC2 together — truthfulness and silence are one problem, not two.
4. AC4, proven by the inversion that previously survived.
5. AC6 mutation, byte-identical restore, anchor verified as matched.
6. Re-run both suites; report counts.
7. **Git endpoint: COMMIT and PUSH `build-015/b15-15-board-truth`. No PR. Do NOT touch `main`. Do NOT
   merge.**

Return: the parked-state enumeration, what you changed, the inversion proof, both mutation directions
with the sha256 pair, suite counts, and anything you refused.
